newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees lower chip sales continuing.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees lower chip sales continuing.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc said it expects to post lower year-over-year semiconductor sales and orders for a few more quarters, although the rate of decline is expected to decrease.

In the company's 10-Q filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday, Motorola said this will continue to hurt profitability in its semiconductor sector, as order backlog fell significantly versus last year.

"It is anticipated that year-to-year semiconductor sales and order growth comparisons are likely to remain negative for a few more quarters, although the rates of decline are expected to lessen," Motorola said in the filing.

On October 8, the day after Motorola reported lower third quarter earnings, company officials had said they expected lower year-over-year industry sales. A spokesman for the company confirmed on Wednesday that Motorola's sales and orders are also expected to continue lower on a year-over-year basis.
"This will continue to place significant pressures on semiconductor profitability, as order backlog has decreased significantly compared to 1995," the company said in the filing.

Last month, Motorola reported its semiconductor sector essentially broke even in the third quarter. Sales in the sector were $1.85 billion versus $2.28 billion in the third quarter last year. The company reported overall earnings of $0.34 a share versus $0.81 last year, in part because of pressure in the chip industry.
Motorola said it is taking steps to cut costs in the semiconductor sector and others, including job cuts and halting building projects.

Late Monday, the Semiconductor Industry Association said its book-to-bill ratio, which measures new orders compared with shipments, rose to 1.10 in October from a revised 0.98 in September, marking the first time it has been over 1.0 since December 1995.
Shares of Motorola closed unchanged at 51-7/8.
